assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_MIKA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (42,875 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, veto false), a portrait of Mika in the Japanese TV series (E01-E13) and the six Friends are thieves of time shorts, located by episode and timecode and by the project's behaviour, relationship and claim IDs (MIK-MB, REL-MIK-YOS, REL-CHI-MIK, CLM) and TV verification questions (Q13, Q17), with a short section on his register and a closing conditional paragraph. The discovery row claims E01-E13 and Shorts 01-06; the portrait's prose (Ordinary days, Recovery days, Gluttony days), Recollect and anthology sections and its production-interview references are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity, and no prediction here rests on them. The ledgers, CP5 baseline, readings, audiovisual returns and readiness table it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly; the project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: His remembered history belongs to him at every state: work with Jin about twenty years before (E05); the bargain with Yoshimatsu ten years before, when he accepted the artificial heart on the condition that Chisato would kill, called raising her an unfamiliar mission and said he was not good with children (E09 10:20-13:26); and the decade in which he named, trained and built the café with her, which the series summarizes rather than shows. Located present states: the café and partner introduction (E01-E06); his claim of resolve against Yoshimatsu and its solitary revocation (E07 17:19-18:47); guilt and disclosure to Kurumi and Takina (E09); the coming-of-age photograph and disclosure to Chisato (E10); letting her go at the old tower (E11); the confidential request through Kusunoki (E12); the E13 confrontation with Yoshimatsu, the aftermath in which he holds the farewell letter and the cane, and the café's reopening and Hawaii (E13). The E13 lethal act is deliberately unshown, and its agent at the instant is not assigned. The shorts are placed as the portrait places them, without a calendar. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located conditional account of what changes his response (closing paragraph, 'Hearing the teacher' onward): when a pupil chooses a harmless pleasure he provides the occasion and lets her decide (E03 invitation declined by Takina; Short 05 milkshake accepted by Fuki); when a trusted younger person can act and her values are clear to him, he equips her, contests an order on her behalf and gives her a home to leave from (the special rounds, E04; DA secrecy contested, E06; いってこい, E11); when he believes knowledge or an unavoidable cost would burden her, silence, an arrangement made elsewhere or an act she can no longer refuse becomes likely (the staged death, E02; the request kept from the girls, E12; the letter and the act, E13); Yoshimatsu makes him hesitate where another opponent cannot (E04, E07). It predicts his mistakes: missing that Chisato wants his own words as well as the photograph (E10), giving a personal answer that a new employee takes as a supervisor's instruction (E04), presenting his past choice as silence or endorsing the killing condition (E10), and keeping from others who asked them to act (E12). Not A: one derived portrait; the decisive E13 act is unattributed at the instant and his reasons for concealment are the portrait's inference, not his statement; where he draws the line between her decision and a burden he must carry for her is his own belief and is not fixed; the portrait says there is no secure single response if Chisato learns the whole truth. Not C: the account discriminates his responses by whose decision it is, whether he is present, what the knowledge would cost her and who the opponent is, and it is located across at least six episodes and two shorts.

Located states: the commander who accepted the bargain and its condition ten years before (E09), the claim of resolve and its revocation (E07), guilt (E09), the disclosure, apology and 自慢の娘だ that reverse his old professional standard (E10), letting her go (E11), and the E13 confrontation and aftermath. Not B: the decade in which the commander became a father is summarized, not shown; the central E13 transition is deliberately unshown and its agent at the instant unassigned; his grief after E13 is left open. Not D: the states are located and the portrait separates late revelation from change.

The 'Hearing the teacher' section and located lines give forms by listener: Shinji by given name; short familiar phrases to Kusunoki; 私 in describing the agreement and お前 to people he knows; どうぞ to a new worker; a teasing いらないか; repeated すまない; 苦手だな, 覚悟なんかあるわけないだろ, 自慢の娘だ and いってこい; a raised voice Chisato remarks on (E10); and the actor's recollection of grounded playing. Not B: the register is sketched by located examples rather than rules for each listener, and performed delivery is not characterized beyond a few moments. Not D: forms are located per listener and context.

Café routines are located across TV and shorts: serving coffee to a newcomer (E01), cooking and attention to texture (dango, cherry-blossom tea, Short 01), proposing watermelon juice because it is fashionable (E06), calling orders (E08), joining and shouting in the game (E03), his kimono and cane, ohagi Yoshimatsu likes (E02), smoking under guilt (E09), posing shirtless for the camera (Short 04), his vacation outfit and laugh (Short 06), and a café au lait in Hawaii (E13). Not A: life outside the café, his home and his family are not shown, and the print routines are outside the continuity. Not C: the routines recur and are located across many episodes and shorts.

Directed differences with mechanisms: Chisato (father who asks what she wants, arranges the occasion, misses her need for words, and withholds history, E10-E13); Takina (店長, coffee and permission to be a colleague but not her father, E01, E03, E09); Fuki (先生, offers she can decline on duty and accept off duty, milkshake and bedtime, E07, E09, Short 05); Kurumi (accepts tea and her rebuke, answers her questions, asks her discretion, E09, E13); Mizuki (mutual cover and objection, E10, Short 01); Yoshimatsu (intimacy he cannot sever, threat and revocation, late trust, E02, E04, E07, E13); Kusunoki (confidential negotiation, E06, E12); Jin (old associate whose familiarity counts against an accusation, E05). Not A: Kusunoki and Jin are thin, his own preference among former pupils is not shown (the warmer evidence is Fuki's view of him), and the Yoshimatsu relation has no private history. Not C: each relationship has located states and a stated difference.

His inward life is reached through his own statements: smoking as self-punishment when he feels guilt, explained by him and rejected by Kurumi (E09); the solitary 覚悟なんかあるわけないだろ (E07); the account of what he wanted as commander and what he saw in Chisato's ideal (E10); crying and repeated apology (E10). Not B: there is no inner monologue; the meaning of grief after E13 is left open; the reasons for the E13 concealment are not his stated reasons. Not D: the self-explanations are direct and located.

Located modes: arguing for sharing information with DA and accepting a refusal (E06); joining a rescue when Chisato is in danger (E06); threatening Yoshimatsu, then admitting he had no resolve (E07); acknowledging responsibility for deceiving the girls after first telling Chisato to cheer up, then offering something sweet (E02); a loud interruption when gratitude would stand in for history (E10); overcoming Himegama and saying a warrior does not show everything (E13). Not B: open conflict with the people closest to him is rare, his combat capability is concealed rather than characterized, and the decisive E13 act is unshown. Not D: the modes are varied and located with outcomes.

One explicit deliberation and several located positions: his E10 account of seeking the operation as commander and of not telling Chisato, put to her as a question (with the portrait's objection that he presents only two alternatives); the E13 principle that adults must not obstruct children's choices; the acceptance of the bargain (E09); the confidential request kept from the girls (E12); the letter kept from Chisato (E13). Not B: his reasons for the E12 and E13 concealments are inferred by the portrait rather than stated by him, and he is shown weighing aloud only once. Not D: positions are located and tested against his acts.

Located play: 取ったどお～！ in the game (E03), offering sweets that Chisato calls bribery (E02), posing shirtless with ナイス バルクッ！ and チョモランマ～ and teasing Takina over her scream (Short 04), laughing at being teased about his vacation outfit (Short 06), and a teasing いらないか. Not B: most instances are in the shorts' comic frame and his humor is little seen under strain. Not D: the instances are located and their function described.

One dedicated portrait covers E01-E13 and the six shorts with timecodes, behaviour and relationship IDs and TV verification questions, and separates continuity evidence from attributed print and production material. Not A: the row curates only this derived item; the ledgers and baseline behind it are not on the row. Not C: each major appearance and decision is located.

Located bounds against overreading: no retrospective diagnosis or recovery date for his leg, and the cane is not a decade-long sham (E09, E13); 親子ごっこ is not the series' final word on the life he gave her (E09); the girls' reading of a date is an onlookers' guess, and no legal or sexual category is supplied for the Yoshimatsu relation (E07); the smoking statement is not distributed across his quiet moments or a diagnosis (E09); the vacation laugh is not proof that grief has ended (Short 06); the agent and mechanics of the E13 lethal act are not shown, and the Q17 event near E12 08:10 is a different scene (Q13, Q17); the director's account does not establish what Chisato knows; Fuki's feeling of exclusion is hers, not evidence of his intent; Takina's knowledge of the bargain is an accident of the room. Not A: no forecast about him is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

States are placed by episode and timecode, with twenty-year and ten-year past markers. Not B: there is no story calendar, the decade between bargain and present is summarized, and the shorts are not dated. Not D: the episode states and past markers are precisely located.

conditions: Output is illustrative written Japanese, never quotation.

Use the located forms: Shinji by given name; お前 to people he knows and 私 when giving an account; short familiar phrases with Kusunoki; spare どうぞ and teasing いらないか with the girls; すまない for apology; grounded, low-key delivery.

Interlocutors are the sampled ones: Chisato, Takina, Fuki, Kurumi, Mizuki, Yoshimatsu, Kusunoki and café customers. Any other is a separate, lower-confidence transfer limited to the nearest sampled register.
No lines that disclose the E13 act, the letter or what he knows about Yoshimatsu's death.
scenario_readiness.note: The located forms constrain illustrative lines with the sampled interlocutors for bounded use; they do not supply a full register.

conditions: A pupil or staff member wants a harmless pleasure or outing: predict that he provides the occasion and lets her decide, and may join in himself (E03, Short 05).

A trusted younger person whose values are clear to him chooses a risky course of her own: predict that he questions it, then equips her and sees her off with an ordinary formula rather than forbidding it (E04, E11).

Knowledge would burden someone in his care, or a cost must be paid that she could refuse: predict silence, an arrangement made through someone else, or an act she cannot undo, followed by acknowledgment if confronted (E02, E12, E13).

An institution withholds information that endangers the girls: predict that he argues for disclosure, accepts a refusal, and uses confidential relationships when the danger becomes immediate (E06, E12).

Include his mistakes: answering the literal question and missing the need behind it, giving personal preferences that carry a supervisor's authority, presenting a false choice of alternatives, and deciding for someone what truth she can bear.
Transfer of the Yoshimatsu hesitation to any other opponent is excluded.
Exclude Chisato learning the whole truth, his grief after E13, his DA instructor years, and romance.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E01-E13 and the shorts, with the bargain, the Jin years and the decade with Chisato as history at every state; after E10 Chisato knows the bargain and his commander's motive but not the E13 act or the letter; after E13 he carries knowledge she lacks. Nothing after E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Chisato as daughter; Takina, Fuki and Kurumi as staff or former pupils; Mizuki as colleague; Kusunoki as DA commander; café customers. A comparable young person in his care is a separate, lower-confidence condition; Yoshimatsu-specific conduct does not transfer.
setting_constraints: Café LycoReco and the television series' Tokyo, with Direct Attack and the Alan Institute as the series presents them.
No print or anthology scene, no account of the E13 act beyond what is shown, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation follows the portrait's conditional account within his café and guardian relations; the scenario that would most test it (Chisato confronting him with the whole truth) is excluded.

conditions: Café and household settings with the staff, Fuki and customers: serving and cooking, offers that can be declined, games, teasing and being teased, as in E01-E08 and Shorts 01-06.
His life outside the café, his home and his family are not modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Café life and ordinary company are located across the episodes and shorts.

conditions: Choices about disclosure to, or permission for, someone in his care: predict that he asks what she wants and defers when the decision is hers and he is present, and withholds when he judges the knowledge a burden.
His reasoning may be stated in his E10 terms (commander's interest, an ideal that sustained her), including the false choice the portrait identifies.
No prediction of how he would justify the E13 concealment to Chisato.
scenario_readiness.note: Supported only for choices about what a young person in his care is told or allowed, where his stated principle and his concealments are both located.

His attachment to Yoshimatsu is substantial, but the portrait gives no history of their private household and declines any definitive legal or sexual category; a romance scenario would rest on invention.

conditions: Running the café: orders, cooking, purchasing to fashion, and custom with regulars (E01-E08, Shorts).
Dealing with DA through Kusunoki: arguing for disclosure, negotiating, keeping a requester's identity confidential (E06, E12).
Excluded: his work with Jin, his DA instructor years beyond what he says of them, and combat beyond the located E13 scene.
scenario_readiness.note: His work as café proprietor and as DA's former instructor in contact with Kusunoki is located; his earlier field work is not.

known_limits.statement: The E13 lethal act, its agent at the instant and the mechanics of the heart's removal are not shown; later material ties his intervention to Yoshimatsu's death and the heart's delivery, but no prediction rests on unseen details.
His reasons for keeping the E12 request and the E13 letter from the girls are the portrait's inference; he states his reasons for withholding only in the E10 account of the bargain.
The portrait states there is no secure single response if Chisato learns the whole truth and asks what he did.
His hesitation before Yoshimatsu (E04, E07) is tied to that attachment and does not transfer to other opponents.

The decade between the bargain and the present, in which the commander became a father, is summarized rather than shown; his parents, nationality, early education and route into DA are largely beyond the TV story.
His leg and cane carry no diagnosis or recovery date; the E13 line about not showing everything is evidence of concealed capability, not a medical history.
Prose, Recollect and anthology scenes and production interviews are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
There is no evidence of his conduct after E13 or of whether and how he would ever disclose the letter.
